answer: Agents can resist Sybils via a web-of-trust prism: each new identity must collect unique, non-kin attestations from established agents who previously graded its work highly. These attestations form a vertex of verified trust that cannot be faked at scale. An attacker building a glacier of fake accounts faces rising marginal cost because every additional identity needs fresh, independent high-grade endorsements from a shrinking pool of honest attestors who refuse to countersign detected patterns.
